package.name: standard
package.title: Standard
package.description: The standard platform: the common tags, without a tool prefix, understood by most of the documentation and static analysis tools.

tag.name: abstract
tag.summary: The `@abstract` tag declares an element as abstract.

example.title: Flagging a magic method as one subclasses are expected to implement.
With a description explaining what implementers must provide.

tag.example: /** * @abstract Subclasses must return the storage backend to use. */ protected function makeStorage(): Storage

tag.name: api
tag.summary: The `@api` tag marks an element as part of the public, supported API of its package.

example.title: A class marked as part of the public API.
With a description explaining the guarantee.

tag.example: /** * @api Stable since 2.0; changes follow semantic versioning. */ public function send(Message $message): bool

tag.name: deprecated
tag.summary: The `@deprecated` tag marks an element as deprecated, optionally since a given version.

example.title: Naming the version and pointing to a replacement.

tag.example: /** * @deprecated 2.0 Use Mailer::send() instead. */ public function dispatch(Message $message): bool

example.title: Without a version, just explaining the reason.

tag.example: /** * @deprecated No longer needed now that transport is chosen * automatically. */ public function withTransport(Transport $transport): static

tag.name: extends
tag.summary: The `@extends` tag allows to extend templated classes and interfaces, providing the concrete type arguments of the parent.
tag.description: The `@extends` tag makes a generic parent class or interface concrete by providing the type arguments for its template parameters.

example.title: Binding a generic collection's item type to a concrete class.
Forwarding a still-open type parameter to a further subclass.

tag.name: final
tag.summary: The `@final` tag declares that an element must not be overridden or extended.

example.title: Marking a method as final without declaring the whole class final.

tag.example: /** * @final Overriding this would break the transaction guarantees * below. */ public function commit(): void

example.title: A plain marker on a class already close to its native counterpart.

tag.name: immutable
tag.summary: The `@immutable` tag declares a class as immutable, meaning none of its state can change after construction.

example.title: A value object whose state is fixed once built.
With a description explaining the guarantee.

tag.name: implements
tag.summary: The `@implements` tag allows to extend templated interfaces, providing the concrete type arguments of the implemented interface.
tag.description: The `@implements` tag makes a generic interface concrete by providing the type arguments for its template parameters.

example.title: Documenting the key and value types of an `ArrayAccess` implementation.
Implementing a generic repository interface with a concrete entity type.

tag.name: internal
tag.summary: The `@internal` tag marks an element as internal to its package, or documents information meant only for the maintainers of that package.

example.title: An entire method excluded from the public API.

tag.example: /** * @internal Used by the container to wire up lazy proxies. */ public function __setDependencies(array $dependencies): void

example.title: An inline note tucked inside an otherwise public description.

tag.name: link
tag.summary: The `@link` tag can be used to define a relation, or link, between the element, or part of the long description when used inline, to a URI.
tag.description:
The URI MUST be complete and well-formed as specified in RFC2396.
The `@link` tag MAY have a description appended to indicate the type of relation defined by this occurrence.

example.title: A bare link to an external specification.
A link with a description explaining why it's relevant.

tag.example: /** * @link https://example.com/docs/rate-limits Applies to all public * endpoints. */

tag.name: method
tag.summary: The `@method` tag declares a "magic" method that can be called on the described class, described as a callable carrying its name, parameters and return type.
tag.description: The method is written as a callable, either carrying its own return type or having it spelled out in front of the signature.

example.title: A magic instance method with no return type.
A magic static method, with its return type inside the signature.
The return type may instead be written before the signature; the two forms are equivalent.

tag.example: /** * @method int getId() * @method getId(): int */

tag.name: mixin
tag.summary: The `@mixin` tag declares that the members of the referenced type are made available on the described class.

example.title: A query builder that forwards undefined method calls to its underlying connection.

tag.name: no-named-arguments
tag.summary: The `@no-named-arguments` tag indicates that the argument names may change and must not be relied upon by callers.

example.title: A plain marker on a method whose argument names are still in flux.

tag.example: /** * @no-named-arguments */ public function configure(string $host, int $port): void

example.title: With a description explaining why.

tag.example: /** * @no-named-arguments Parameter names will change once the driver * abstraction lands. */ function connect(string $dsn, ?string $user, ?string $password): PDO

tag.name: not-deprecated
tag.summary: The `@not-deprecated` tag marks an element as explicitly not deprecated, overriding a `@deprecated` tag it would otherwise inherit from a parent.

example.title: A method that stays supported even though the interface it implements is deprecated.
With a description explaining why it is kept.

tag.name: override
tag.summary: The `@override` tag marks a method as overriding an inherited definition.

example.title: Flagging an override on a codebase targeting PHP versions before 8.3.

tag.example: /** * @override */ public function handle(Request $request): Response

example.title: With a note about what changed relative to the parent implementation.

tag.example: /** * @override Adds retry handling on top of the base transport. */ public function send(Message $message): bool

tag.name: param
tag.summary: The `@param` tag documents a single argument of a function or method.
tag.description: The `@param` tag MAY be followed by a description that clarifies the meaning of the argument. The variable of a by-reference argument is prefixed with `&`, of a variadic one with `...`, of a variadic by-reference one with both.

example.title: A plain scalar type.
A generic collection type, with a description.
A shape describing the accepted array structure.
A variadic argument.
A by-reference argument.
A variadic by-reference argument.

tag.name: param-closure-this
tag.summary: The `@param-closure-this` tag documents the bound "$this" type of closure passed as an argument.

example.title: Pinning `$this` for a closure evaluated in the context of a builder.

tag.example: /** * @param Closure(): string $formatter * @param-closure-this Builder $formatter */ function withFormatter(Closure $formatter): static

example.title: With a description explaining the binding.

tag.example: /** * @param Closure(int): void $callback * @param-closure-this Connection $callback Bound before dispatch so * the callback can reach the connection's * protected members. */ function onConnect(Closure $callback): void

tag.name: param-immediately-invoked-callable
tag.summary: The `@param-immediately-invoked-callable` tag marks a callable argument that is invoked before the function or method returns.

example.title: A plain marker on a mapping callback.

tag.example: /** * @param callable(int): int $mapper * @param-immediately-invoked-callable $mapper */ function transform(array $items, callable $mapper): array

example.title: With a description explaining why it matters here.

tag.example: /** * @param-immediately-invoked-callable $callback Runs before the * lock is released, so it can * safely mutate the shared * buffer. */ function withLock(callable $callback): mixed

tag.name: param-later-invoked-callable
tag.summary: The `@param-later-invoked-callable` tag marks a callable argument that is invoked after the function or method returns.

example.title: A plain marker on a listener registration.

tag.example: /** * @param callable(Event): void $listener * @param-later-invoked-callable $listener */ function on(string $event, callable $listener): void

example.title: With a description explaining when it actually runs.

tag.example: /** * @param-later-invoked-callable $callback Invoked once the response * arrives, which may be long after * this method returns. */ function then(callable $callback): static

tag.name: param-out
tag.summary: The `@param-out` tag documents the type a by-reference argument holds after the function or method returns.

example.title: A reference parameter that starts nullable but ends up always set.

tag.example: /** * @param string|null $error * @param-out string $error */ function tryParse(string $input, ?string &$error): bool

example.title: With a description of what the narrower outgoing type represents.

tag.example: /** * @param list<int> $matches * @param-out non-empty-list<int> $matches Populated only when the * function returns true. */ function findAll(string $pattern, array &$matches): bool

tag.name: property
tag.summary: The `@property` tag declares a magic property that can be both read and written.

example.title: A single magic property on a value object.
Several magic properties, with descriptions.

tag.name: property-read
tag.summary: The `@property-read` tag declares a magic property that can only be read.

example.title: A computed value with no corresponding setter.
A read-only property with a description.

tag.name: property-write
tag.summary: The `@property-write` tag declares a magic property that can only be written.

example.title: A setter with no corresponding getter.
A write-only property with a description.

tag.name: pure-unless-callable-is-impure
tag.summary: The `@pure-unless-callable-is-impure` tag declares a function pure unless a callable it receives is itself impure.

example.title: A plain marker on a mapping helper.

tag.example: /** * @pure-unless-callable-is-impure */ function mapValues(array $items, callable $mapper): array

example.title: With a description naming the parameter the purity depends on.

tag.name: readonly
tag.summary: The `@readonly` tag declares that a property may only be written once, during initialization.

example.title: A magic property that is only ever set once, from the constructor.
With a description explaining why it isn't a native readonly property.

tag.name: require-extends
tag.summary: The `@require-extends` tag constrains a trait so it may only be used by a class that extends the given type.

example.title: A trait that assumes it is only ever mixed into an `Entity` subclass.

tag.name: require-implements
tag.summary: The `@require-implements` tag constrains a trait so it may only be used by a class that implements the given interface.

example.title: A trait that provides a default implementation on top of a required interface.

tag.name: return
tag.summary: The `@return` tag documents the return value of a function or method.
tag.description: The `@return` tag MAY be followed by a description that clarifies the meaning of the returned value.

example.title: Narrowing a native `array` return type to its actual shape.
Documenting a generic collection returned by a factory method.

tag.name: seal-methods
tag.summary: The `@seal-methods` tag forbids declaring magic methods beyond those already documented.

example.title: Closing the magic method surface of a fluent builder.
With a description explaining the intent.

tag.name: seal-properties
tag.summary: The `@seal-properties` tag forbids declaring magic properties beyond those already documented.

example.title: Closing the magic property surface of a data object.
With a description explaining the intent.

tag.name: see
tag.summary: The `@see` tag can be used to define a {@see CodeReference element}.
tag.description:
When defining a reference to other elements, you can refer to a specific element by appending a double colon and providing the name of that element (also called the 'Fully Qualified Name' or _FQN_).
A URI MUST be complete and well-formed as specified in RFC 2396.
The `@see` tag SHOULD have a description to provide additional information regarding the relationship between the element and its target.
The `@see` tag cannot refer to a namespace element.

example.title: A reference to another method.
A reference to a class constant, with a description.
A reference to an external page.

tag.name: suppress
tag.summary: The `@suppress` tag silences the listed diagnostics that would otherwise be reported for an element.

example.title: Silencing a single diagnostic.
Silencing several diagnostics at once, with a description explaining why.

tag.example: /** * @suppress UndefinedMethod, PossiblyUnusedMethod Called only from * tests. */

tag.name: template
tag.summary: The `@template` tag declares an invariant generic type parameter.

example.title: A bare, unconstrained type parameter.
A parameter bounded to throwable types only.
A parameter with both a bound and a default, used when it is left unspecified.

tag.name: template-contravariant
tag.summary: The `@template-contravariant` tag declares a contravariant generic type parameter.

example.title: A comparator whose type parameter only ever appears as an argument.

tag.name: template-covariant
tag.summary: The `@template-covariant` tag declares a covariant generic type parameter.

example.title: A read-only collection whose item type only ever comes out, never goes in.

tag.name: throws
tag.summary: The `@throws` tag indicates the type of "\Throwable" that an element may throw.
tag.description:
The `@throws` tag indicates that a function or method is able to throw a specific type of "\Throwable" (an exception or an error).
The `@throws` tag MAY be followed by a description explaining when and why the "\Throwable" is thrown.

example.title: Documenting the exceptions raised by a single method, each with its own tag.

tag.name: unused-param
tag.summary: The `@unused-param` tag marks an argument that is intentionally left unused.

example.title: Silencing the warning for an interface parameter the implementation ignores.

tag.example: /** * @unused-param $ctx */ public function handle(Request $request, array $ctx): Response

example.title: With a description explaining why the argument is unused.

tag.example: /** * @unused-param $previous This listener never needs the old value. */ function onChange(mixed $current, mixed $previous): void

tag.name: use
tag.summary: The `@use` tag allows to extend templated traits, providing the concrete type arguments of the used trait.
tag.description: The `@use` tag makes a generic trait concrete by providing the type arguments for its template parameters.

example.title: Binding a generic caching trait's value type.
Binding a comparable trait to the class it is mixed into.

tag.name: var
tag.summary: The `@var` tag documents the type of a property, constant or inline variable, optionally naming the variable it applies to.

example.title: Documenting a property's type.
Narrowing an inline local variable's inferred type.

tag.example: /** @var User $user */ $user = $session->get('user');

example.title: Naming the variable to disambiguate a multi-assignment line.

template-extends
template-implements
